clue.text: Vulgar, unfriendly, making petty complaint

parts.note: common in the sense of coarse or low-class
a cold manner is an unfriendly one

explanation.surface: Someone coarse and frosty is making a fuss about something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cold is a minor ailment, and 'complaint' is a standard word for an illness, so petty complaint describes it.

clue.text: Male caught twice — second time collared by fine

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: something collared is held round the neck, so it sits enclosed by what follows

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
the second use of the abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket note about a man dismissed twice, the second time pinned down by a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The first C stands at the front; the second C goes inside OK, giving O-C-K after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is the male of a bird, especially the domestic fowl.

clue.text: He may captivate Spaniards at random, avoiding northern resorts

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
avoiding something means leaving it out, so one letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern; it is removed

explanation.surface: Someone charms Spanish people haphazardly while steering clear of resorts in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At random' looks like an anagram signal but is the fodder; 'resorts' is the real signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the star bullfighter, a figure who holds Spanish crowds spellbound in the ring.

clue.text: Senior funds conversion of a lodge with B&B in France

indicators.note: a conversion changes the form of something, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a pension is the French name for a guesthouse or bed-and-breakfast

explanation.surface: Retirement money is spent converting a lodge into a French guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The state retirement payment in Britain was long called the old-age pension, money for senior citizens.

clue.text: Bono and Tom Cruise, maybe short for stars?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: examples of famous people
second meaning: the clipped informal word for celebrities

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' seems to tease the height of the singer and the actor, but it means abbreviated: the answer is the clipped form of a word for famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebs is the informal shortening of celebrities, and the singer and the actor are both examples of famous figures.

clue.text: Miss exit in error

parts.note: to exit is to leave
out means mistaken, as in 'your sums are out'

explanation.surface: Someone missed the exit by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out something is to omit or skip it, which is one sense of the verb miss.

clue.text: Internet joke the writer repeated

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me
the same word given a second time

explanation.surface: An online joke that its author keeps posting.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a humorous image or phrase that spreads widely online.

clue.text: Come out with former partner, one tucking into shellfish

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: something tucking into food goes inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A night out with your ex, who is eating seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out with' looks like going out on a date with the ex, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to blurt or cry out words, just as one comes out with a remark.

clue.text: They may choose English Conservative to get in or Attlee, unexpectedly

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other
something that happens unexpectedly is out of its expected order, so letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An election where voters choose between an English Tory or Labour's Attlee, with a surprise result.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the Labour Prime Minister who beat Churchill unexpectedly in 1945, which makes 'unexpectedly' sit naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters, the people who choose representatives.

clue.text: Keep filed: a ticket partly required for return

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards
partly means only a portion of the words is used, so the answer lies inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An instruction to file away a return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep filed' reads like a filing instruction, but 'Keep' alone is the definition, the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest tower of a castle, and a citadel is likewise a fortress stronghold.

clue.text: One's failure leaves politicians etc speechless

definitions.text: One's failure leaves politicians etc speechless

parts.note: surface reading: some failure leaves public figures lost for words
setter's reading: the thing that fails is the device scrolling a speaker's script, so without it they literally have no speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'Speechless' seems to mean stunned, but it means left without the prepared text that a screen was showing them.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is a teleprompter, the screen that shows presenters and politicians their script as they speak.

clue.text: Kid filmed scene they cropped — one in a Disney cartoon

indicators.note: a cropped thing has had its end trimmed off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a take is one filmed version of a scene
taken as written, then shortened
Mickey Mouse, Disney's best-known cartoon character

explanation.surface: A child filmed a scene that was then cut, with a part in a Disney cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to tease. 'Take the mickey' is British slang for mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease them, which is what taking the mickey means in British slang.

clue.text: 'Shadows split!' — Express tip

parts.note: to dog someone is to shadow or follow them
to split is to break
an express train is a fast one

explanation.surface: A newspaper tip-off: the Shadows have split up, says the Express.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shadows were a British pop group and the Express is a British newspaper; 'tip' here means a mess, as in a rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's breakfast is British slang for a complete mess, and a tip is an untidy, messy place.

clue.text: Sweet but heartless, betrays soldiers

indicators.note: heartless means without a heart, so the central letter is removed

parts.note: a sweet is the dessert course
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: Someone who is sweet but cold-hearted betrays others.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats is the nickname of a British army division, so its members were soldiers.

clue.text: Centre of feud: guy perhaps in international group

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word
a guy is a rope that holds a tent steady

explanation.surface: A guy at the heart of a dispute within an international body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe can mean the European Union, a grouping of nations, in British political usage.

clue.text: Client reversing before MoT successfully parks inside

indicators.note: a car reversing goes backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
something parked inside sits within the words, so the answer is concealed in them

parts.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word, the whole middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A garage client backs in and parks after the car passes its MoT.
explanation.walkthrough: An MoT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is someone who buys goods or services, which is what a client is.

clue.text: Give bear mashed waffle

indicators.note: mashed food is pulped out of its original form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Feed a bear a mashed-up waffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waffle' looks like the batter cake to mash, but it means wordy talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbiage is excessive wordiness, which is exactly what waffle means as a noun for empty talk.

clue.text: Threaten bother after having wind up

parts.note: to wind up is to end
to bother or annoy is to anger

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to cause trouble after winding a person up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the annoying word behind the closing one.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, which is to threaten it.

clue.text: Raising scores in police dept gets go-ahead

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters up, so they read bottom to top
in places one word inside another

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
scores of things means many

explanation.surface: A rise in crime figures in the police department gets the green light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go-ahead' looks like permission, but here it is the adjective for an energetic, enterprising person.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead firm or person is enterprising and energetic, which is what dynamic means.

clue.text: Loner using hi-tech to follow Queen, arrested by Her Majesty?

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so this piece is held inside the other

parts.note: HM is the abbreviation for Her Majesty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's royal cipher
IT, information technology

explanation.surface: A recluse uses technology to keep up with royal news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To follow' places the technology pair after the royal sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone in seclusion, the very picture of a loner.

clue.text: Spy trapped by 007's boss, a sort of red

indicators.note: a trapped thing is caught inside something, so it sits within the other pieces

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories
a spy is a secret agent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy caught by James Bond's chief turns out to be a Red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sort of red' suggests a communist in the spy story, but it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, so it is one shade of red.

clue.text: Go round in jeans, upset about weight

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so its letters read from bottom to top
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Levis are a well-known brand of jeans
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Someone spins round in their jeans, worried about their weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to turn or pivot about a point, which is to go round.

clue.text: Alley cats' throwdown?

parts.note: surface reading: a fight between stray cats in a back street
setter's reading: the alley is a bowling lane, the 'cats' are players, and the throwdown is literally hurling a ball to knock pins down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alley cats' suggests strays, and 'throwdown' a fight; read literally they are lane players throwing a ball down the alley.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is played on long alleys by rolling a ball to topple ten skittles, so a competition there is a throwdown.

clue.text: Detached place with sea view on all sides?

definitions.text: Detached place with sea view on all sides?

parts.words: Detached place with sea view on all sides?
parts.note: surface reading: an estate agent's advert for a detached house with views of the sea all round
setter's reading: a place cut off from the mainland, surrounded by water

explanation.walkthrough: The estate-agent language of a 'detached' property misleads; the place is detached from land itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a piece of land surrounded by sea, so every side has a sea view.

clue.text: Bullets turned in, along with a pungent gas

parts.note: ammo, short for ammunition, covers bullets

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned
taken as written; the a before 'pungent gas' belongs to the definition

explanation.surface: Bullets handed in alongside a nasty-smelling gas.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' does double duty in the surface; the wordplay needs a separate A, taken from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a colourless gas with a sharp, choking smell, as in smelling salts.

clue.text: They raided six royals

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
kings are royals

explanation.surface: Raiders attacked six members of a royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings were Norse seafarers famous for raiding the coasts of Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Notice broken cask

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put together differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a barrel that has split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb meaning spot, but it is the noun for a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting your notice means being dismissed from a job, which is getting the sack.

clue.text: Last chance to acquire exotic fruit — group get on the phone first

indicators.note: on the phone words are only heard, so their sound matters, not their spelling

parts.note: a cell is a small group, as of activists
to get something can mean to buy it
a date is the fruit of a tropical palm

explanation.surface: A last chance to buy some exotic fruit, as long as a group phones in first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts the two spoken words ahead of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-by date is the last day a shop may sell an item, so it marks the final chance to acquire it.
